solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: What could be small Scottish swallow of old

wordplay.note: the Scots word for small is SMA, and SMA could be written as the letter A placed by SM

explanation.surface: A wee Scottish bird of olden times, perhaps a little swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: ABYSM read as A BY SM is a recipe for SMA, the Scots for small. 'Swallow' is the noun for a deep gulf, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word for a bottomless pit or chasm, and a swallow in the old sense is a gaping gulf.

clue.text: Weak-willed deserter a senior officer's locked up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something locked up is held inside, so one piece sits within the officer's title

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief
a rat deserts a sinking ship

explanation.surface: A feeble deserter has been imprisoned by the general.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking self-control or strength of resolve; a rare word for someone without mastery over their own impulses.

clue.text: Blister oozed endlessly on top of boot

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a wound that oozed bled

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down entry is its first letter

parts.note: the opening letter of boot

explanation.surface: A blister weeping fluid over the top of someone's boot after a long walk.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the boot's first letter goes underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A small bubble or vesicle of fluid on the skin, a common synonym for a little blister.

clue.text: Noisy bird upset two fairies

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so each word is read backwards

parts.note: a fay is a fairy
an elf is the second fairy

explanation.surface: A raucous bird has disturbed a couple of fairies.
explanation.walkthrough: Each fairy is reversed on its own; reversing the pair together would give the wrong order.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect name for the green woodpecker, called after its loud laughing cry.

clue.text: Gleaning I support in season

indicators.note: placed in means the first pieces sit inside the word for season

parts.note: to season food is to spice it
taken as written
a leg supports a table

explanation.surface: A farmworker gathering leftover grain says they lend a hand during the harvest season.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection or anthology of gathered pieces, literally a gleaning of ears of corn, from Latin spicilegium.

clue.text: Stone in wall level with side of quadrangle

parts.note: on a par means level
a pane is one side or panel of a square figure

explanation.surface: A building stone sits flush with one edge of a college courtyard.
explanation.walkthrough: A quadrangle is the enclosed courtyard of a college; here it is just a four-sided figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A through-stone or bondstone running the full thickness of a wall, also spelt parpen.

clue.text: Brilliant soft local substance used in making glass

parts.note: in gem cutting a pear is a pear-shaped brilliant
lash is a dialect word meaning soft or slack

explanation.surface: A dazzling soft material from nearby goes into glassmaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' marks a dialect word, the usual crossword signal for a regional sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude potassium carbonate, an alkali historically used as a flux in glassmaking and soap.

clue.text: Half sent up evangelical Catholic logician

indicators.note: in a down entry sent up means raised so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the first half of the word for the Catholic
a Marist is a member of a Catholic missionary order; this is the rest of that word

explanation.surface: A Catholic missionary sends up a philosopher by half.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of MARIST is turned round; the rest stays in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Petrus Ramus, the French scholar who reformed Aristotelian logic.

clue.text: Opening in India a friend set up around acting

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means raised so the word reads upwards
around means wrapped about another letter

parts.note: a pal is a friend
A is short for acting, as in a rank

explanation.surface: A friend sets up a play at the start of a trip to India.
explanation.definitionFit: The slow improvised introductory section of a raga in Indian classical music.

clue.text: Managed lifting cross under our church portico

indicators.note: in a down entry under means placed below, so the cross goes after the possessive word
lifting a word in a down entry makes it read from the bottom up

parts.note: ran a business means managed it
as in 'the' or 'our' firm
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A cross carried under the porch of our church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' places the cross below the other pieces in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The antechamber or porch at the western entrance of an early church, before the nave.

clue.text: Deposit in a bank paid after this gets reported as prank

indicators.note: reported means said out loud, so the combination is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an escapade is a prank; said aloud it can be heard as two words, the second being paid
taken as written, and removed

explanation.surface: Money is paid into a bank deposit, which turns out to be a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says that putting 'paid' after this word sounds like a prank: ESKER + PAID sounds like ESCAPADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A long winding ridge of gravel and sand laid down by a glacial stream, so a sediment forming a bank.

clue.text: Trap fastening beside swarm never has succeeded

indicators.note: never having something means it is taken out of every word it was in

parts.note: a clasp is a fastening
a nest of insects can be a swarm
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A trap with a fastener next to a swarm of bees that never worked.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird-catcher's net that is sprung shut by pulling a cord, a type of fowling snare.

clue.text: In the end completely out of time, sadly

indicators.note: completely out of means every instance is removed, not just one

parts.note: at last means in the end
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Eventually we ran right out of time, unfortunately.
explanation.definitionFit: An interjection of regret, used like 'unfortunately' to introduce bad news.

clue.text: Give an update to reference to magnetism

parts.note: ref is short for reference
it means sex appeal or personal magnetism

explanation.surface: An instruction to revise a citation about magnetism.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'to' means placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhaul and re-equip a ship or building, bringing it up to date.

clue.text: Take in land once which African explorer may have owned?

parts.note: to own something is to admit it, as in saying 'I'm ...'
Mungo Park explored the Niger in West Africa

explanation.surface: Acquiring territory in the past, which an explorer of Africa might have claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mungo Park could have owned up with 'I'm Park'; 'owned' means admitted, not possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb for enclosing ground as a park or pound, so taking land in.

clue.text: What's rolled during tetanic rictus, rolled inwards

indicators.note: rolled means turned over, so the letters run the other way
during means within the span of the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A medical image: the jaw clenched in a tetanus grin, curled inward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolled' appears twice: first as the turning signal, then within the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Coiled from the tip towards the base, as a young fern frond is when unfurling.

clue.text: Foolishness in backing artificial intelligence course out of term

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the little word turns round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: term here means end or limit, so the final letter goes

parts.note: AI is the usual abbreviation
a course of lectures is a series

explanation.surface: Folly in supporting a course on AI that runs outside term time.
explanation.definitionFit: A French borrowing for silliness or naive simplicity, a piece of foolish behaviour.

clue.text: Inform houses in advance of cases of fungus

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside

parts.note: to inform is to tell
I is a recognised abbreviation for in
A is short for advance

explanation.surface: Tell the householders ahead of time about mould.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole adjectival phrase 'of cases of fungus'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to telia, the spore-bearing pustules of rust fungi, which hold the winter spores.

clue.text: Group of small creatures diascope blows up

indicators.note: something blown up is shattered, so its letters land in a new order

parts.note: a projector for slides, taken as written

explanation.surface: A slide projector enlarges the image of some tiny insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows up' looks like magnifying with the projector, which suits the surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of barklice and booklice, tiny insects, given the -idae family ending.

clue.text: What scrapes vehicle reversing? My getting in one

indicators.note: a vehicle reversing goes backwards, and so does its word

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: getting in means another letter goes inside the exclamation

parts.note: lor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone backs their car and exclaims as it scrapes something.
explanation.definitionFit: A prehistoric flint scraper, a tool used for scraping hides.

clue.text: Got out of condition like a northern waster?

indicators.note: out of here means outside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: got and had both mean possessed
a state is a condition

explanation.surface: Someone who got out of shape, like a good-for-nothing from up north.
explanation.walkthrough: A waster in Scots is a fish-spear, not an idler; that is what makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Spear-shaped, like a leaf with a pointed tip and flared basal lobes, so resembling a spear.

clue.text: Scotch stupid clue leading to rising trend?

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
the answer is itself a clue: a letter placed on another word

explanation.surface: A stupid clue that leads to an upward trend.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is itself a little clue: split it into a letter, the word 'on', and four letters, and in a down entry 'on' means placed above, so it spells the rising word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for dazed or stupefied, hence dull-witted and slow.

clue.text: Bit of tack gives way, thus having to replace half of it

indicators.note: replacing means one piece is swapped out for another

parts.note: a roof that gives way caves in
so means thus
one of the two letters of the word it

explanation.surface: A piece of riding equipment breaks, so half of it must be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is horse-riding gear such as saddles and bridles.
explanation.definitionFit: A noseband used in training and lungeing horses, one item of a horse's harness.

clue.text: Squirt well quiet about serious blow

indicators.note: about means surrounding another piece

parts.note: 'so' and 'well' both open a sentence
KO is a knockout
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A fountain gushes quietly before a hard blow of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quiet' joins at the end, after the container is built.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a spurt or jet of liquid, also used as a verb for squirting.

clue.text: Gene variant partly responsible for parallel evolution

indicators.note: partly means only part of the following words is used

parts.note: the letters run from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: A biology statement: one gene version is partly behind parallel evolution.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the alternative forms of a gene that can occupy the same position on a chromosome.

clue.text: Surrounded drunk given to ranting away

indicators.note: away means that piece is sent off and removed

parts.note: hammered is slang for drunk
to ham is to overact, ranting on stage

explanation.surface: A drunk, surrounded by people, starts ranting.
explanation.definitionFit: An old verb mere meant to bound or form a boundary, so this past form means bounded or enclosed.

clue.text: African cloth jumper dispensing with fleece mostly

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so a piece is dropped

parts.note: a kangaroo is a famous jumper
to rook someone is to fleece them; mostly drops its last letter

explanation.surface: An African garment made like a jumper without most of its wool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater; it is the animal. 'Fleece' is a verb meaning swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A brightly printed cotton fabric worn wrapped as a garment by women in East Africa.

clue.text: Typeface left over in abandoned cans

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the reshuffled word
abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

parts.note: taken as written
L is short for left
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A printed label is all that remains on some discarded tins.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif font family designed by William Caslon in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Mineral zero energy drink got backing, low in calories

indicators.note: going backwards means the opening pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: O looks like zero
E is the symbol for energy
ale is a drink
lite is the marketing spelling for low-calorie

explanation.surface: A zero-calorie energy drink has found financial backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of nepheline, a greasy-looking silicate rock mineral, also called eleolite.

clue.text: Time following festival, as and when

parts.note: ut is Latin for as
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Holiday time after a festival, whenever it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: The octave of a church feast, the eighth day or week-long period after a festival.

clue.text: Past trouble with Norman over scornful term for woman

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the combined pieces read backwards

parts.note: noy is an old word for annoyance or trouble
Nor is short for Norman

explanation.surface: Old disputes with a man called Norman over a rude insult to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A Shakespearean insult for a mangy or scabby woman, used in Macbeth by the witches.

clue.text: Get wet sheltered by one Scottish ridge

indicators.note: sheltered by means held within the other piece

parts.note: ae is Scots for one
to ret flax is to soak it

explanation.surface: Get soaked while sheltering behind a Scottish mountain crest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp narrow mountain crest between two glacial valleys, a knife-edge ridge.

clue.text: Ingredient for nog one's put in? Rum's close to it

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the ingredient

parts.note: egg goes into eggnog
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Making eggnog: one ingredient goes in, then the rum is added.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is not the spirit but a Hebridean island; its neighbour in Scotland's Small Isles is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides, lying just south-east of the island of Rum.

clue.text: Secure round a docked missile installation at the base

indicators.note: round means surrounding the following pieces

parts.note: to bar a door is to secure it
taken as written

indicators.note: docked like a tail, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a silo houses a missile

explanation.surface: Guard a missile silo at a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Situated at or relating to the bottom part of an organ or structure, as in anatomy.

clue.text: Time traveller carries advanced electronic instrument

indicators.note: carrying means holding another letter inside

parts.note: Doctor Who is the time-travelling hero of a long-running British TV series
A is short for advanced
E is short for electronic

explanation.surface: A time traveller carries some advanced electronic gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden tool with a blade set at right angles, pulled towards the user, so a hand implement.

clue.text: Go off most unattached female misses

indicators.note: missing something means going without it

parts.note: free means unattached
F is short for female

explanation.surface: The most single woman misses out and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect verb for bacon or meat turning rancid, so spoiling or turning bad.
